dictionary.BR Realistic: Ground Realistic Battle Rating. BR = (economicRank // 3) + 1 plus 0 / .3 / .7.
dictionary.Unit Class: wpcost unitClass: light/medium/heavy tank, tank destroyer, SPAA, etc.
dictionary.Weapon Systems: Count of distinct gun files on the vehicle, including MGs and smoke launchers.
dictionary.Largest Caliber (mm): Biggest calibre across all of the vehicle's weapon systems.
dictionary.Reload Time (s): Gun file base reload. Crew skill and ace bonuses are applied by the engine and are NOT included.
dictionary.Rate of Fire (shots/min): Derived: 60 / shotFreq. For single-shot cannons read Reload Time instead.
dictionary.Vehicles Using: Distinct vehicles referencing this gun file.
dictionary.Min BR (RB): Lowest Realistic BR among vehicles that can field this. The downtier case.
dictionary.Median BR (RB): Median Realistic BR — the honest placement figure.
dictionary.Stock Shell: Yes = available before researching any modification.
dictionary.Ammo Family: Derived from bulletType by prefix. Raw bulletType is kept alongside for auditing.
dictionary.Modification Key: The key inside the gun file that holds this shell. Matched against the vehicle's modifications block to decide availability.
dictionary.Muzzle Velocity (m/s): bullet.speed for shells; rocket.maxSpeed or startSpeed for missiles.
dictionary.Pen Source: Where the penetration figure came from. Three values; see READ ME. Blank pen cells mean the engine computes it at runtime and the number is not in the files.
dictionary.Hit Power: bullet.hitPower — internal post-penetration damage scalar, not a real-world unit.
dictionary.Fuse Delay (m): bullet.fuseDelayDist — distance travelled inside the target before detonation.
dictionary.Fuse Sensitivity (mm): bullet.explodeTreshold — minimum armour needed to trigger the fuse.
dictionary.Is Missile: Yes when the shell carries a nested rocket block (ATGM or SAM).
dictionary.Operated Distance (m): rocket.operatedDist — range over which a SACLOS operator can still steer.
dictionary.Control Cone FoV (deg): guidance.controlConeFov — the cone the missile must stay inside to keep command guidance.
dictionary.Pen @10m (mm): Penetration at 10 m. For chemical rounds this is constant across all distance columns by design.
dictionary.Casing AP Table (raw): Raw armorpower table. On chemical rounds this is casing/fragment penetration, not the shaped-charge jet. Audit only.
dictionary.Vehicles With This Ammo: Distinct vehicles that can research or start with this round.
dictionary.Stock Ammo: Same as Stock Shell, on the link table.

readme: War Thunder — Ground Forces: vehicles, guns and ammunition
1237 ground vehicles with a BR and at least one weapon.
3956 gun-shell combinations, of which 296 are guided missiles.
1,237 of 1,248 ground units in wpcost matched. The 11 misses are SAM fire-control vehicles with no weapon of their own, plus one event car.
START HERE — 'HOW MANY OF WHAT SHOULD I TAKE?'
One row per vehicle. Full capacity, protected-rack capacity, a recommended total, and the split. This is the answer a new player wants.
The same recommendation broken out one row per shell, with a plain-English 'Why' for each.

1) Rank the gun's anti-tank rounds by penetration. 2) Make the best one the bulk of the load. 3) Reserve ~12% for high explosive if the gun has one, for open-topped and light targets. 4) Reserve ~18% for a gun-launched ATGM if present - high penetration but slow, so a handful, never the magazine. 5) Add up to 3 smoke. 6) Add a backup anti-tank round at ~25% only when it kills differently from the primary, i.e. it has explosive filler and the primary does not.

Recommended Total = the protected-rack count when the vehicle has one, otherwise full capacity. Rack data comes from ammoStowages: racks flagged fatalExplosion false are the protected ones. 123 of 1,201 vehicles have a protected rack.
Most vehicles. Carrying less still reduces how much can cook off, but the files give no safe threshold, so the guide does not invent one. The Ammo Rack Risk column says so per vehicle.

Per vehicle. 'Ranked on penetration' = every anti-tank round on that gun has a penetration figure. 'Mixed long-rod and full-calibre' = the ordering across those two shell types is the least certain part. 'PARTIAL' = some rounds fell back to muzzle velocity.
THE PENETRATION PROBLEM — READ THIS BEFORE USING ANY PEN NUMBER
Tells you where the number came from. There are three cases and they are NOT interchangeable.
550 shells. The file carries an ArmorPower table by distance. These numbers are exact.

536 shells (HEAT, HEAT-FS, HESH, ATGM). Penetration comes from cumulativeDamage.armorPower and does not fall off with range, so every distance column repeats the same value. That is correct behaviour, not a copy error.

648 shells. Computed with DeMarre coefficients found in the game files themselves - demarrePenetrationK, demarreSpeedPow, demarreMassPow, demarreCaliberPow - using damageCaliber (the penetrator rod diameter, e.g. 22 mm inside a 120 mm shell), not the gun calibre. Checked against 69 long-rod shells that also carry an explicit table: median ratio 1.20, p10-p90 0.81-1.31. Treat as plus or minus about 25 percent.

1,992 shells. Same formula, but the output needed a scale factor of 3.64 to match known values, and that factor is fitted on ONLY 2 observations. The absolute millimetres here are weak. Use the ordering, not the number.
342 shells. No coefficients anywhere in the files. Blank, not guessed.

The raw DeMarre output before any scaling. Within one gun every shell of the same penetrator type shares the same unknown scale, so this column orders them correctly even where the absolute millimetres are shaky. The loadout ranking uses it as a tiebreak. Do NOT compare it across different guns.

Mostly inline in each shell's damage.kinetic block in groundmodels_weapons. Some bulletTypes (apds_fs_long_l30_tank) have no projectile_types file of their own and fall back to the base type with the variant suffix stripped.
How to close the gap properly
Scrape the in-game stat card for a few hundred shells and refit. That is the only way to pin the full-calibre scale factor and cut the error bar.
For chemical rounds this is the casing/fragment penetration from armorpower. It is small (single-digit mm) and is NOT the shaped-charge jet. Kept for auditing only.
GAME values, not real-world values. Gaijin retunes every patch; BRs move fastest.
Ammunition availability per vehicle comes from matching the gun's shell keys against the vehicle's 'modifications' block. A shell the vehicle cannot research will not appear in Vehicle x Ammo.
Stock Shell = Yes marks the round available before any modification is researched.
Reload time is the gun file's base value. Crew skill, ace status and autoloader rules are applied by the engine and are not reflected here.
Nation is the tech-tree country from wpcost, not the vehicle's country of origin.

Armour values are NOT in this dataset. They live in the per-vehicle damage models, a separate and much larger extraction. The loadout guide therefore ranks shells in the abstract, not against the armour you will actually meet at that BR.

Slope Effect Reference holds the angle multipliers from damage_model/slope_effect.blkx, keyed by shell preset and calibre-to-armour ratio. They are NOT applied in the ranking - applying them needs a target armour set, which is the next decision.
BR = (economicRank // 3) + 1, plus 0.0 / 0.3 / 0.7 for remainder 0 / 1 / 2. Verified: T-34 (1941) 4.0, Pz III J 2.7, M4 Sherman 3.7, T-80BVM 12.7.
Min / Median / Max BR of the vehicles that can load that round. A shell has no BR of its own.
